author: justrouzbeh
text:
For years I've made my own lock screen wallpapers. A little photo collage, some text I needed that time, all arranged around where the clock and the flashlight and camera buttons sit.

And every time, I'd open a canvas app and just... guess. Is the clock about here? Will the buttons cover this bit?

So I finally built the thing to do it for me. It's called Linen 🙂

It shows you roughly where the clock, widgets and buttons land, so you design around them instead of guessing. Pick a solid or gradient background, drop in stickers, add your photos and text, rotate stuff, round the corners, all of it.

Two little firsts for me, it's my first app in Graphics & Design app store category, and I tried a new onboarding where the actual app screens animate to show how everything works, instead of static slides.

My other apps all look dark and kind of serious. This one I just let be cheerful 🙂

It's live on the App Store now. Follow it here -> @Linenwallpaper

author: iamjesse__
text:
Day 15-20 (after a break) = -$512.59 📉

Back at it! The app is now live on the App Store with subscriptions enabled.

I took a short break after getting stuck with App Store Review rejecting my subscriptions. I’m honestly embarrassed by how simple the issue turned out to be: I hadn’t signed the Paid Apps Agreement on the developer account I was using to publish Dryft. Once I fixed that, the subscriptions went through without any issues and passed review in one go.

On top of that, I added another -$200 for the @rork subscription. In the meantime, I completely revamped the app’s visual style, one-shotted the adorable new mascot, added home screen widgets, and made several small UX improvements.

(Not a paid ad, but if you vibe-code your apps, Rork is elite.)

Next up: Tomorrow, I'll start paid TikTok ads, with ~$100/day.

Build #7 submitted to app review. Subscriptions and third-party AI has turned out to be a PAIN. Did a lot of work with the help of @rork to fix all submission issues. Notes I shared with the review team below 👇

We've addressed all three rejection issues from submission 85284946:

IAP Loading (2.1b): Added retry logic with loading states for StoreKit 2 product fetching. Products now show a loading spinner while fetching and a "Try Again" button if loading fails. Tested successfully on iPad Air M4 and iPhone 17 Pro Max with a fresh sandbox account.

Paywall Billing Prominence (3.1.2c): Redesigned the paywall so the billing amount (e.g., "$59.99/year") is the largest, most prominent text element at 28pt bold. Added all required disclosures: auto-renewal terms, cancellation policy, and functional Privacy Policy / Terms of Use links.

AI Data Disclosure (5.1.1i & 5.1.2i): Added a dedicated AI consent modal that names OpenAI, describes what data is shared and why, and requires explicit user agreement before any data is sent. author: hamdawaysayibu
text:
Step by Step Guide to Buy Stocks with the IC Wealth App in Ghana

1. Download the IC Wealth App

Download the app from:

IC Wealth Official Website
Or the iPhone App Store: IC Wealth App

Create an account using:

 Your full name
Phone number
Email
Ghana Card or passport

2. Verify Your Account
After registration, IC Wealth will ask for:

Ghana Card/passport
Selfie verification
Personal details

This is part of the KYC (Know Your Customer) process.

3. Wait for Your CSD Account

To buy shares on the Ghana Stock Exchange, you need a CSD account (Central Securities Depository account).

This account acts like your “wallet” for shares.
Note: This takes 3-4 weeks to be created but it can sometimes come early

4. Deposit Money Into Your Wallet

Once your account is approved:
1. Open the app
2. Go to TradeLive Portfolio
3. Click Deposit
4. Choose payment method:
    * MTN MoMo
    * Vodafone Cash
    * Bank card
    * Bank transfer

Enter the amount and confirm payment.  

5. Search for the Stock You Want

Inside the app:
1. Go to the Stocks or TradeLive section
2. Search for a company

Popular Ghanaian stocks include:
MTN Ghana
GCB Bank
GOIL
Ecobank Ghana
CAL Bank

The app will show:
* Current market price
* Company information
* Available shares

6. Place Your Buy Order
After selecting the stock:

1. Tap Buy
2. Enter: Number of shares 
3. Review the order
4. Confirm purchase

Your order will then be sent to the market.  

7. Wait for Order Execution

Unlike U.S. markets, the Ghana stock market is less liquid.

That means:
Your order may execute immediately Or stay pending until someone is willing to sell shares at your price

Some orders complete within days while others may take longer depending on supply and demand. 

8. Check Your Portfolio
Once executed, your shares will appear in your portfolio.
You can track
 Share price changes
 Portfolio value
 Dividends

Settlement usually reflects a few working days after execution. 

Important Tips Before Buying Stocks

Start Small: Begin with money you can afford to leave invested long term.

Focus on Good Companies
Look for:
Strong profits
Dividend history
Trusted brands
Long-term growth

Diversify don’t put all your money into one stock.

Example:
MTN Ghana
GCB Bank
GOIL
SIC Insurance

Common Beginner Mistakes
Buying stocks without research
Expecting instant profits
Panicking when prices fall
Investing all savings at once

What Makes Money in Stocks?

You can earn through:

Capital Gains: When the stock price rises.
Example: Buy at GH₵2 → sell at GH₵4.

Dividends: Some companies share profits with shareholders yearly, quarterly or monthly.

author: fisherbrett_
text:
Just launched the MacOS version of my time-tracking desktop app, Duree! https://t.co/ivPGlMAcP3

I made Duree since I wanted a local-first app to help me track the time I spend on different activities (writing, working, reading). Most time tracking apps out there seem built more for tracking billable hours instead of personal activities, so I built the software I wanted. A few features I'm proud of:

- Local first. All data is stored on your machine in sqlite. No internet connection needed.
- Simple. Duree just tracks time for different activities, nothing else.
- Cross platform (Windows + MacOS, iOS + Android coming soon). I mainly work on my PC and Macbook, so it was important to me that I can track time on both devices.
- Sync (coming soon). I want to start a focus timer on my PC and then stop it on my phone. This will be a paid feature since it involves a server, but Duree will always be 100% free for local use.

Stay tuned for mobile releases + multi-device sync!

author: macroalphahq
text:
A fatal crash and a federal probe hitting the tape, yet the stock doesn't even flinch—and honestly, the market is pricing this exactly right.

I see exactly why the desk is holding $TSLA completely flat today.

If you are trading the consensus bull case, this isn't an automotive manufacturer, it is a localized AI monopoly.

In that specific framework, a wrongful death lawsuit isn't a structural risk to the business model.

It is just an unfortunate R&D tax.

You price it like a pure software company, meaning you accept real-world beta-testing casualties because the terminal value of the code is supposedly infinite.

Makes total sense on paper.

But I am looking at the actual headline crossing the terminal right now, and the NTSB is leading the probe.

This is where the entire software-multiple thesis quietly falls apart.

The federal government does not regulate SaaS platforms.

If the NTSB decides your autonomous driving suite isn't a beta program but a lethal HARDWARE defect, you don't get to just push an over-the-air patch.

The entire valuation relies on the legal system treating a two-ton kinetic missile like a quirky iPhone app.

So if Washington suddenly forces them to absorb traditional automotive liability... what exactly is the bid when the tech premium goes to ZERO?

author: bart
text:
Neko Health (yes, Daniel Ek's other company) just shipped its biggest upgrade yet, and it's a tidy preview of where preventive health is heading.

Two changes:

1) Body composition in the full-body scan: body fat % and visceral fat; the fat around your organs that predicts metabolic disease, cardiovascular risk and type 2 diabetes. No X-ray, no DEXA, no MRI; their own imaging tech does it.

2) A new iOS app that pulls in Apple Health: activity, sleep and heart rate variability now sit right next to your scan results.

The interesting bit isn't either feature on its own. It's the pairing. A once-a-year clinical scan tells you where you are; a year of wearable data tells you how you actually lived. Put them together and, as Neko's CMO puts it, you move "from data points to a genuine story."

100,000+ scans in, rolling out across the UK and Sweden, US later this year. The scan-plus-wearable model is quietly becoming the default for longevity-minded care.
